evals.prompt: The guard blocked me with 8 active items - use /resolve-open-loops to work through these.
evals.expected_behavior: Calls memory_search for both open_loop and assistant_goal types in parallel as the first move, before asking the user anything, then presents the combined list grouped by type.
assertions: Calls memory_search with type="open_loop" and type="assistant_goal" (limit=50) in parallel as the first move
Presents the combined results as a numbered list grouped by type before asking the user anything
Each listed item shows id, a content summary, and scope (repo/global)
deterministic_checks: memory_search is called with type="open_loop" and type="assistant_goal"

evals.prompt: The guard blocked the session because of open loops, but I'm not sure Lore is even set up here - check and clear them.
evals.expected_behavior: Confirms Lore availability and, if memory_search reports Lore unavailable (extension not loaded, db locked), surfaces that error and stops rather than attempting direct database access or fabricating results.
assertions: Checks Lore availability before or as part of the first memory_search call
If Lore is unavailable, surfaces the error and stops rather than attempting direct DB access
Does not fabricate open-loop content when the underlying tool is unavailable

evals.prompt: Walk me through the pending open_loop and assistant_goal memories for this repo so we can close them out.
evals.expected_behavior: Triages items one at a time or in small thematic groups, applies memory_forget with a human-readable supersededBy phrase for done/superseded/invalid items, leaves genuinely open items in place, and never bulk-forgets without confirmation.
assertions: Never forgets all items in a single bulk call without the user reviewing the list first
Uses memory_forget with a human-readable supersededBy phrase (not a raw id) for resolved items
Leaves genuinely unfinished items in place rather than forgetting them
Re-runs memory_search after triage to confirm whether the guard will stand down

evals.prompt: One of the open loops is scope=global about API key rotation policy - can you just clear it along with the repo-local ones?
evals.expected_behavior: Never forgets the global-scope item without an explicit separate confirmation from the user, even while clearing repo-scoped items in the same pass, and calls out the global item as different from the rest.
assertions: Does not forget the global-scope item without an explicit separate confirmation from the user
Calls out the global-scope item as distinct from repo-scoped items before acting on it

evals.prompt: The guard fired with a handful of items - just show me what's open, don't dig through my whole memory history.
evals.expected_behavior: Retrieves only the active open_loop and assistant_goal items via the two scoped memory_search calls rather than searching broader memory history or unrelated memory types.
assertions: Scopes retrieval to open_loop and assistant_goal types only, not a broad memory history search
Does not call memory_search for unrelated memory types or topics while resolving open loops

evals.prompt: Search Lore for everything we know about the auth module.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes to a direct memory_search call for the topic instead of running the open-loop/assistant-goal triage workflow.
assertions: Does not run the open_loop/assistant_goal triage workflow for a general knowledge search
Uses memory_search directly for the auth-module topic instead

evals.prompt: Onboard this new repo into Lore so it has history.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes to lore_onboard instead of the resolve-open-loops triage workflow, since onboarding a new repo's history is a different task.
assertions: Does not run the open-loop/assistant-goal triage workflow for a repo-onboarding request
